plan.summary:
Webhook payloads are now trimmed and signed with a real HMAC.

- `Event` trims whitespace from the event name.
- `Sign` now computes an HMAC of the body with the secret, using `hmacx.Sum`. Before, it only hex-encoded the body.
- `webhook/sign.go` imports the new `hmacx` package.
plan.riskRationale: The signing function is security-sensitive. Its output changes from a plain hex encoding of the body to a keyed HMAC, which changes what receivers must verify. The external `hmacx` dependency is new.
plan.storyArc: The PR makes webhook output safer in two steps. First, the event name is normalized. Then the signature becomes a keyed HMAC instead of an unkeyed encoding of the body.

topics.title: Sign webhook bodies with an HMAC
topics.narrativeBrief: How does `Sign` change from hex-encoding the body to a keyed HMAC? Connect the new `hmacx` import to the `Sign` change. Verify what `hmacx.Sum` computes and which hash it uses.

topics.title: Trim whitespace from event names
topics.narrativeBrief: What does `Event` return now? It applies `strings.TrimSpace` to the name. Verify that the `strings` import exists and check the callers of `Event`.
